### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | APA Publishing (covers Psychiatric Services as an APA journal) requires full disclosure of any generative-AI use in the manuscript text/methods and in the cover letter. Generative-AI tools cannot be listed as authors; authors remain fully responsible for all AI-assisted content; AI-generated images are prohibited; AI output may not be cited as a primary source. This is a disclosure-and-restriction policy (not an outright ban, not fully open) — hence leniency 2 (permitted only under disclosure + real restrictions on images/citation). Could not directly load the live ps_ifora page (403 Forbidden to WebFetch) to confirm this exact page still states the same wording as of 2026-07-13, so treat leniency/gate as APA-Publishing-wide policy inferred to apply to this journal, not independently verified on the journal's own current page. |
| **Source URL** | https://psychiatryonline.org/ps/ps_ifora (page fetch blocked 403; facts triangulated via WebSearch snippets of this same page, plus general APA Publishing generative-AI policy referenced across APA journals) |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): No journal-specific preprint statement was retrievable for Psychiatric Services itself (ps_ifora page blocked). Sister APA journal American Journal of Psychiatry explicitly states posting preprints is not prior publication and asks authors to disclose differences from the preprint and link it. Given APA Publishing operates policy consistently across its journals, this is LIKELY analogous for Psychiatric Services but is not confirmed on the journal's own page.
